From the moment I resolved to make this place my home, I planted a stand of desert poplars. 
A name grew with them—Poplar Bazaar. 
That restless heart, once doomed to wander, has slowly found its calm. 
One by one, I learned the names of everyone in Poplar Bazaar and at Jade Gate Pass— 
including the general's. 
He carried heavy burdens, often weighed down by worries for Poplar Bazaar itself. Pointing to the wells we dug together, he said this place reminded him of Hexi. 
But a handful of scattered wells will one day run dry. 
His dream was to link this land to Hexi, all the way to the Tang Empire's heart—to turn this barren desert into a land lush with water and grass. 
When that day comes, Hexi will flourish once more, and Jade Gate Pass will belong firmly to the realm. 
The trading routes will reopen, and I will lead my caravans—openly, with pride—back to Chang'an. 

Over time, the poplars have grown tall, their seeds carried on the wind, spreading the legend of this golden land far beyond. 
As for me, I've patiently built my fortunes, waiting for the day when the caravans return to Chang'an.
